title: Credibility Assessment of Implicit Finite Element Models for Distal Radius Plate Screw Angulation Effects Under NASA-STD-7009A
runhead: Distal radius plate angulation FEA credibility
device: Volar locking distal radius plate with variable-angle screw options

models.name: Model A: Patient-Specific Volar Plate Assembly
models.what_it_computes: Conical seat contact pressure and plate-hole plastic strain versus screw angulation; screw bending moment and axial force; local screw–bone interface micromotion in cortical and trabecular regions.

models.name: Model B: Generic Bone–Plate Construct with Homogenized Bone
models.what_it_computes: Global construct stiffness and load redistribution with angulation; screw–bone shear stress envelope and predicted margin to interfacial yield; distribution of force among screws under eccentrically angled trajectories.

models.name: Model C: Plate–Screw Conical Seat Submodel (Motif)
models.what_it_computes: High-fidelity conical seat contact map, peak principal stress at plate-hole rim, and screw-head seating force path under extreme angulations; sensitivity of local fields to friction and seating torque.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 1: Plate-hole conical seat overstress
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Overstress at the conical seat can initiate hole ovalization and microcracking, degrading the plate–screw interface and risking loss of alignment.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 2: Screw–bone interface degradation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Off-axis screw trajectories elevate shear and micromotion at the bone interface, promoting loosening, cutout, and early fixation failure, especially in low-density bone.

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–7 Credibility Index for each model × mechanism pair; an overall index is computed as the arithmetic mean across factors.
